question: Which physical and visual characteristics, such as shape, size, materials, color, face, and anthropomorphic elements, are considered in the design of interaction with social robots?
description: Relevant: passages describing or analysing the robot's physical/visual design (morphology, size, materials, color, face, anthropomorphic or zoomorphic features) and why it was chosen or how it affects interaction. Not relevant: purely software/behavioral details with no appearance component, or generic mentions of 'a robot' without design description.
sub_queries: robot body shape and size design
robot materials, texture and color
robot face and facial features design
anthropomorphic and zoomorphic appearance of social robots
effect of robot morphology and visual appearance on user perception

extraction_fields.name: finding
extraction_fields.description: Short statement of the physical/visual characteristic considered (e.g. 'rounded body, 30 cm tall, LED eyes').

extraction_fields.name: evidence_quote
extraction_fields.description: Verbatim passage from the paper that supports the finding. Do not paraphrase.

extraction_fields.name: page
extraction_fields.description: Page number where the passage appears, for manual verification.

question: Which communication modalities and strategies are used in the design of interaction with social robots, including speech, voice, language, gestures, movements, touch, light, and sound?
description: Relevant: passages describing how the robot communicates with or receives communication from people (verbal and non-verbal channels, their design, and the strategy behind them). Not relevant: communication between robots, or low-level networking/protocol details.
sub_queries: robot speech and voice characteristics such as prosody, pitch and tone
natural language dialogue strategies in social robots
robot gestures and body movement for communication
touch and haptic interaction with social robots
light and sound cues such as LEDs and non-verbal sounds as robot communication
multimodal communication in human-robot interaction

extraction_fields.name: finding
extraction_fields.description: Short statement of the modality and strategy used (e.g. 'LED color patterns to signal listening state').

extraction_fields.name: evidence_quote
extraction_fields.description: Verbatim passage from the paper that supports the finding. Do not paraphrase.

extraction_fields.name: page
extraction_fields.description: Page number where the passage appears, for manual verification.

question: How are emotions, expressiveness, and personality incorporated into the interaction design and communicated by social robots during interaction with people?
description: Relevant: passages describing how emotion, expressiveness or personality is designed, modelled, implemented or displayed by the robot, and how it is conveyed to the user. Not relevant: emotion recognition of the human alone, with no robot-side expression or design.
sub_queries: emotion expression in social robots through face, body and voice
robot personality design and traits
expressiveness through movement, color, light and sound
affective response and emotional models in robots
user perception of robot emotions and personality

extraction_fields.name: finding
extraction_fields.description: Short statement of how emotion, expressiveness or personality is incorporated and communicated (e.g. 'extraverted personality conveyed via larger gestures and louder speech').

extraction_fields.name: evidence_quote
extraction_fields.description: Verbatim passage from the paper that supports the finding. Do not paraphrase.

extraction_fields.name: page
extraction_fields.description: Page number where the passage appears, for manual verification.

question: Which methods and instruments are used to evaluate the characteristics of the interaction design of social robots?
description: Relevant: passages naming or describing the evaluation method (user study design, qualitative or quantitative technique) and the instruments used (questionnaires, scales, interview protocols, behavioral or physiological measures). Not relevant: evaluation of purely technical performance (e.g. latency, recognition accuracy) with no interaction-design component.
sub_queries: evaluation methods for social robot interaction design
questionnaires and scales to assess robot design and perception
user study with social robots: measures and instruments
qualitative evaluation with interviews, observation and thematic analysis
behavioral and physiological measures in human-robot interaction

extraction_fields.name: finding
extraction_fields.description: Short statement of the method and/or instrument used and what it evaluated (e.g. 'Godspeed questionnaire to rate perceived anthropomorphism').

extraction_fields.name: evidence_quote
extraction_fields.description: Verbatim passage from the paper that supports the finding. Do not paraphrase.

extraction_fields.name: page
extraction_fields.description: Page number where the passage appears, for manual verification.

question: What open questions, limitations, and unresolved challenges do the studies identify regarding the design of interaction with social robots, as stated in their discussion, limitations, and future work?
description: Relevant: passages where the authors explicitly state limitations, open questions, research gaps, unresolved challenges or directions for future work related to social robot interaction design. Not relevant: the authors' own results or contributions, and generic motivation in the introduction.
sub_queries: limitations of the study on social robot interaction design
future work and open research directions for social robots
unresolved challenges in human-robot interaction design
lack of long-term studies, small samples and limited generalizability
ethical and technical open issues for social robots

extraction_fields.name: finding
extraction_fields.description: Short statement of the limitation, open question or challenge (e.g. 'no long-term deployment; effects over weeks unknown').

extraction_fields.name: evidence_quote
extraction_fields.description: Verbatim passage from the paper that supports the finding. Do not paraphrase.

extraction_fields.name: page
extraction_fields.description: Page number where the passage appears, for manual verification.
